scenes.heading: Variables
scenes.caption: Variables are names for values. Each name is a label, and the value is whatever is stored under that label at this moment. Almost every program you write is a set of named values being changed on purpose. If the names are clear, the program is explainable.

scenes.caption: Give each value a name that says what it is for. Read a name to get the current value. Assign a new value when the fact changes. Keep one meaning per name. Do not reuse score for a user's email.

scenes.caption: A JWT is a signed token that carries claims, such as a user id and an expiry. Anyone can read the payload. Only the signer can produce a signature that checks out. Servers like them because they can check the signature without a database lookup. The cost is that you cannot easily take one back before it expires.

scenes.heading: Mocking
scenes.caption: Mocking replaces a collaborator, such as a payment service, with a stand-in you control. The test decides what the stand-in returns. It lets you test your logic without calling the real service. It lies if the stand-in drifts away from the real service.

items: Mocking replaces a collaborator, such as a payment service, with a stand-in you control

scenes.caption: Mock at the edge, not inside the function you are testing. Make the stand-in return the case you care about: success, and then one failure. Do not assert the mock was “called” as your only check. Assert the outcome.
